chunks: Saad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from one who narrated to him, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar al-Ja'fi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The servants are closest to Allah and most pleasing to Him when they miss the Proof of Allah, who does not appear to them and they do not know his location, yet in that state they know that the Proof of Allah has not been invalidated nor his covenant broken, so at that time they anticipate relief morning and evening. For the wrath of Allah is most severe upon His enemies when they miss His Proof, who does not appear to them. And He knows that His friends will not doubt, and if He knew that they would doubt, He would not have hidden His Proof from them for even a blink of an eye, and that [doubt] will not be except upon the heads of the worst of people.'

key_terms.حُجَّةُ اللَّهِ: Proof of Allah (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of believers during the occultation of the Imam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the theological concept of *al-ghaybah al-sughra* as a period of divine testing, where the Imam's hidden presence intensifies the believers' spiritual proximity to Allah. It distinguishes between steadfast companions who maintain certainty in the Imam's enduring authority and the 'worst of people' whose doubt triggers severe divine wrath, illustrating the Shi'a view of occultation as a mechanism for purifying faith rather than a cessation of guidance.
